threads.body: `testing` is an instance `@RegisterExtension` field, and the class uses JUnit's default `PER_METHOD` lifecycle. In that setup, JUnit doesn't call class-level callbacks for the extension, so `InstrumentationExtension.beforeAll`/`afterAll` never run. That means `AgentTestRunner.beforeTestClass()` never resets the listener. `afterTestClass()` is also skipped, so the checks for instrumentation errors, advice failures, muzzle failures, and ignored-but-transformed classes don't run, and the metadata flush is skipped. `java-tests.instructions.md` says the extension must be registered "so JUnit invokes its class-level callbacks". The neighboring `AkkaActorTest` uses `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` for this reason.
